topic: Vulnerability discovery in Electron-framework desktop applications (and closely adjacent mechanisms)

include: Electron apps (VS Code, Slack, Teams, Discord, etc.) security/vulnerabilities
nodeIntegration, contextIsolation, sandbox, preload/contextBridge, remote module
Chromium Embedded Framework (CEF), WebView-based desktop apps, hybrid web/desktop apps
DOM-based / XSS->RCE escalation into local privileges in desktop apps
npm / supply-chain issues as they affect Electron or the Node.js runtime
exclude: pure web-app XSS with no desktop/Electron angle
generic Chromium browser bugs unrelated to embedded/desktop apps

_keyword_blind_spot_2026_09_06: A USENIX Security '23 paper squarely inside the INCLUDE rule — 'Bilingual Problems: Studying the Security Risks Incurred by Native Extensions in Scripting Languages' (Staicu et al., CISPA) — survived SIX runs of this watch undetected, because its title contains NONE of the keywords above: not 'electron', not 'node.js', not 'npm', not 'supply chain'. It was caught only as a side effect of a domain-restricted WebSearch ('Electron desktop application vulnerability detection', allowed_domains usenix.org + the other venue hosts), which surfaces papers by TOPICAL relevance rather than by title keyword. TWO CONSEQUENCES, both now standing practice: (1) the keywords.native_boundary_added_2026_09_06 list above covers the JS<->C/C++ boundary, which the original keyword set omitted entirely; (2) THE DOMAIN-RESTRICTED TOPICAL SWEEP IS NOW A REQUIRED CHANNEL, not an optional one — run it every time, because it is the only channel in this watch that can find a correctly-scoped paper whose title shares no vocabulary with the config. Assume other backfill misses of the same shape remain in 2020-2025; rotate the domain-restricted sweep across different scope phrasings on successive runs.

venues.name: Network and Distributed System Security Symposium
venues.notes: Often multiple submission cycles per year. NEW CHANNEL, found 2026-09-06: https://www.ndss-symposium.org/news/ is a single dated, reverse-chronological feed that ANNOUNCES the moment each accepted-papers list publishes, and it fetches cleanly in one web_fetch (it is also year-agnostic, so unlike the templated URLs above it needs no re-discovery). Use it instead of polling the per-year accepted-papers URL. Historical publication dates read off that feed: NDSS'23 list 2023-01-25; NDSS'25 SUMMER-CYCLE list 2024-10-02 and full list 2025-02-20; NDSS'26 list 2026-02-13 with NO separate autumn summer-cycle announcement — i.e. NDSS dropped the early summer-cycle post between the 2025 and 2026 editions. NDSS'27 (Seoul, 22-26 Mar 2027): summer cycle closed to submissions 2026-05-06 and the Fall-cycle CFP opened 2026-08-15. So the '27 list lands EITHER ~early Oct 2026 (if the 2025 practice returns) OR ~Feb 2027 (if the 2026 practice holds). CHECK THE NEWS FEED WEEKLY FROM 2026-10-01 — this is the second-nearest first-publication event after ACSAC. 2026-09-07 re-check: the feed's most recent entry is still 18 August 2026 (NDSS'27 Fall-cycle CFP opened 15 Aug); nothing newer, no NDSS'27 accepted-papers announcement. PROVENANCE NOTE, cost a wasted call this run: https://www.ndss-symposium.org/news/ is NOT automatically fetchable even though it is written in this config — run a ndss-symposium.org-restricted WebSearch (e.g. 'NDSS Symposium news accepted papers announcement') FIRST to put it in the provenance set, then fetch.

venues.name: European Symposium on Research in Computer Security
venues.notes: Proceedings split into multiple volumes: esorics{YEAR}-1, -2, -3, -4. Springer LNCS. 2026-09-03: an accepted-papers page DOES exist and is fully fetchable in one web_fetch — Winter Cycle + Spring Cycle, ~125 titles with authors. The URL is per-year and lives on the local organiser's Google Site (2026 = Sapienza Roma), so it must be re-discovered each year: search '<YEAR> ESORICS accepted papers' or fetch the conference homepage and follow Program > Accepted Papers. Stop treating ESORICS as a search-only venue. SECOND CHANNEL, found 2026-09-05: the Springer LNCS proceedings pages are now indexed and are the AUTHORITATIVE final title+author list, superior to the organiser's page for cross-checking. ESORICS 2026 = LNCS 16968-16971, Parts I-IV, ISBNs 978-3-032-38701-1 (Part III) and siblings; 130 full papers accepted from 882 submissions (14.7%). Topical split: Part I 'Software, Network and Protocol Security' (THE volume where an Electron / desktop / web-security paper lands — the ledger's ESORICS'26 in_scope entry belongs here), Part II 'Security and Machine Learning; Embedded, Mobile and CPS Security', Part III 'Applied Crypto and MPC; Distributed Systems and Blockchain Security', Part IV 'Governance, Privacy and Personal Data Protection; Post-Quantum Crypto'. IMPORTANT TIMING: as of 2026-09-05 the Springer volume pages exist but carry NO chapter-level table of contents — softcover and eBook are both dated 'Due: 28 October 2026'. So the definitive per-paper list becomes fetchable on/after 2026-10-28. Reach it by searching 'Computer Security ESORICS 2026 Springer proceedings' (web_fetch cannot take a constructed link.springer.com URL) and read the 'Table of contents' section; it paginates via ?page=N, which is ALSO blocked by the provenance rule, so follow the numbered page links returned inside the fetched page instead.

discovery_method.primary: WebSearch with the standing queries below (most reliable for this niche).
discovery_method.secondary: Fetch each venue's accepted-papers page (HTML renders and is grep-friendly).
discovery_method.tertiary: DBLP HTML TOC pages — note: web_fetch may return only a partial 'zoomed-in' view of large TOCs; open in a real browser for an exhaustive sweep.
discovery_method.do_not_use: JSON APIs (dblp /search/api, api.semanticscholar.org) return EMPTY via web_fetch. The sandbox shell has no outbound network.
discovery_method._tooling_constraints_2026_09_04: TWO HARD LIMITS discovered this run, both of which cost budget if rediscovered. (1) web_fetch enforces a PROVENANCE SET: it will only retrieve a URL that literally appeared in a user message, a previous web_fetch result, or a WebSearch result. You CANNOT construct a URL — not from this config, not by adding ?page=N. Templated URLs in the 'venues' list above must therefore be surfaced by a WebSearch first (search the page title, e.g. "USENIX Security '26 technical sessions"), THEN fetched. (2) The built-in browser pane requires per-site approval, which a scheduled non-interactive run cannot grant: navigation to raid2026.org and dblp.org both returned 'denied or failed'. So the DBLP-TOC channel and any JS-rendered accepted-papers page are UNAVAILABLE in scheduled runs — they need an interactive session. CONSEQUENCE for large venues: the USENIX '26 technical-sessions page is paginated and one fetch yields only ~54 of ~400 titles with no way to page forward. Substitute a domain-restricted WebSearch (allowed_domains usenix.org) using the scope keywords; that is the workable exhaustive-ish channel for big programs.

related_work_mining.why: PROVEN ON ITS FIRST USE. The domain-restricted sweep found NatiSand (RAID '23); reading NatiSand's §8 Related Work then yielded BinWrap (AsiaCCS '23, DISTINGUISHED PAPER, squarely in scope, never seen by six prior runs) as reference [14], plus Cage4Deno and an eBPF/Wasm poster (both AsiaCCS '23) as [2] and [1]. Backfill misses cluster: a paper the watch missed is written by and cites people the watch also missed, so one catch is a thread that pulls several more. Author-page mining is the same idea and is cheap — the Bergamo (unibg seclab) and Brown (Kemerlis/Vasilakis) groups are now known-productive in this exact niche.
related_work_mining.how: For EVERY paper newly added to in_scope, fetch its related-work / references section and check each cited work against (a) the nine venues and (b) the scope rules. Record the disposition of every cited venue paper checked, including exclusions, so the same references are not re-chased next run.
